title: How Many Exposures Does a World Model Need? Learning Unseen Game Mechanics at Test Time
excerpt: World models enable agents to plan and learn from imagined experience, but in an unfamiliar environment they must learn its mechanics from limited interaction. A mechanic is a rule for how an action or an interaction changes part of the environment. Each occurrence of a mechanic that the model observes is one exposure. We ask how many exposures a world model needs to predict the effects of a new environment's mechanics. We address this question on ARC-AGI-3, a benchmark of interactive games defined by their programs. We introduce MechEval, which labels 69 recurring mechanics across 20 games from these programs. It scores each prediction on the cells the mechanic changes at each exposure. As…

ai.summary: The study measures how many exposure events a world model needs to learn new game mechanics, using the ARC‑AGI‑3 benchmark of interactive games.
ai.why: Insights guide developers on data efficiency requirements for deploying world models in novel environments.

excerpt: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) offer complementary routes to post-training. We introduce Reframe, a post-training framework that treats the observation state, rather than only the output distribution, as an object of alignment. excerpt: State Space Models (SSMs) have emerged as a compelling alternative to Transformers, enabling sequence modeling with constant memory and linear compute. title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
excerpt: Lloyd's k-means algorithm is a long-running standard for clustering, with applications in data analysis, retrieval, quantization and data curation. In this paper, we introduce an exponential moving average optimization procedure for k-means with mini-batch updates, powered by modern deep learning machinery and new insights. We also establish scaling laws on how decay rate and batch size impact final performance. This gives us a formulaic rule to fix them for multiple problem sizes and embedding datasets, without the need for any hyperparameter sweep. The resulting clustering algorithm, coined e-means, is much faster than Lloyd k-means and converges to lower losses, frequently even beating…

ai.summary: The authors propose e‑means, an exponential moving average optimization for mini‑batch k‑means that converges in roughly one‑tenth the epochs of Lloyd's algorithm, with derived scaling laws for decay rate and batch size.

title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
excerpt: We introduce Sage-Taiyi, a metacognition-inspired architecture that uses accumulated scientific understanding to guide what to investigate next and how to investigate it. Through explicit monitoring and control, the system revises its understanding of evidence, assumptions, and unresolved questions, then uses these assessments to adapt research targets and select reusable reasoning methods. On Taiyi-Bench, an AI co-scientist ideation benchmark comprising 265 tasks from 50 papers across ten disciplines, Sage-Taiyi ranks first on all eight metrics of historical rediscovery and open-ended ideation, achieving an Overall score of 54.0 compared with 47.9 for the strongest baseline, AI…

excerpt: Challenging repository-level benchmarks remain limited for many programming language ecosystems, where filtering scarce candidates with ambiguous descriptions or defective tests can discard valuable engineering problems. title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
excerpt: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. We ask whether preserving recovered procedures and decisions improves subsequent independent reproduction. We define a standardized artifact design comprising a refined codebase, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide, and introduce ReproBridge, an agent workflow for constructing these refined reproducible artifacts. title: InfraRSI: Harnessing Recursive Self-Improvement for Training Infrastructure
excerpt: While Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) accelerates isolated algorithm and kernel synthesis, distributed LLM training depends on tightly coupled launch settings, operator kernels, and communication schedules, where single edits often hit out-of-memory (OOM) boundaries, compiler conflicts, measurement jitter, or silent numerical drift. title: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
excerpt: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a standard post-training method for diffusion models, but most RL objectives roll out the current policy at every iteration, and with a many-step sampler these rollouts typically dominate the cost of training. Few-step models cut this cost, yet they model an average velocity over an interval, whereas existing RL objectives are built for an instantaneous velocity with a many-step sampler. We adapt RL objectives to few-step models systematically in three phases, namely a transformation, a decomposition and an adaptation. title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
excerpt: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model on its own responses, guided by a fixed teacher. Such mismatch can destabilize reinforcement learning (RL), but its effects on OPD remain unclear.
